question: What will the Antarctic sea ice extent be on October 10, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Antarctic sea ice extent for 2026-10-10 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I couldn't find anything that settles the question before the cutoff. As of 2026-09-11, Antarctic extent was **17.619 M km²**. Over 2016-2025, extent changed between Sep 11 and Oct 10 by anywhere from **-0.83 to +0.28 M km²**. The average was about -0.24, and the more recent years fell more.

## 1. Resolution source
- **Source:** the NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 daily file, [S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv). I read it directly. It has one value per day in recent years, in millions of km².
- **Latest value as of 2026-09-11: 17.619**, the highest of the season so far. The newest daily value usually goes up the next day.
- **Recent values from the file:**
  - 2026-09-01: 17.415
  - 2026-09-05: 17.404
  - 2026-09-08: 17.460
  - 2026-09-09: 17.568
  - 2026-09-10: 17.565
  - 2026-09-11: 17.619
- **August 2026 path:**
  - 2026-08-07: 16.341
  - Fell to 15.955 on 2026-08-11
  - 2026-08-20: 16.490
  - Fast growth to 17.327 on 2026-08-31

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Ice is usually near its yearly peak in mid-September and then starts to shrink. On 2026-10-10 the value will likely be a few tenths below the peak, but that is not certain.
- 2026-09-11: 17.619 is close to the same date last year (2025-09-11: 17.612). It is above 2023 (17.004) and 2024 (17.209), and below 2016-2022. [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-09-03: NSIDC's post "Arctic zigs; Antarctic zags" said Antarctic ice had an unusually large mid-winter drop over about a week in August. That matches the fall from about 16.34 to 15.96 between Aug 7 and Aug 11. [NSIDC Sea Ice Today](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses)
- 2026-08-19: NSIDC restarted its monthly Sea Ice Today analyses. [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses)
- I couldn't find other dated news about Antarctic ice from before Sep 12.

## 4. Base rates
All values below come from the [NSIDC daily file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv). Units are M km².

| Year | Sep 11 | Oct 10 | Change | Sep-Oct peak (date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | 18.171 | 17.884 | -0.29 | 18.464 (Sep 7) |
| 2017 | 18.014 | 18.089 | +0.08 | 18.145 (Oct 9) |
| 2018 | 17.745 | 18.026 | +0.28 | 18.315 (Sep 30) |
| 2019 | 18.299 | 18.234 | -0.07 | 18.489 (Sep 26) |
| 2020 | 18.829 | 18.659 | -0.17 | 19.062 (Sep 25) |
| 2021 | 18.716 | 17.889 | -0.83 | 18.814 (Sep 1) |
| 2022 | 18.112 | 17.898 | -0.21 | 18.276 (Sep 13) |
| 2023 | 17.004 | 16.508 | -0.50 | 17.109 (Sep 7) |
| 2024 | 17.209 | 16.861 | -0.35 | 17.283 (Sep 15) |
| 2025 | 17.612 | 17.301 | -0.31 | 17.854 (Sep 15) |

- **Change from Sep 11 to Oct 10, 2016-2025:** the average was about -0.24 and the middle value about -0.25. Eight of 10 years fell. For 2021-2025 alone, the average was about -0.44.
- **Applied to 17.619 (simple arithmetic, not a forecast):**
  - The full range of past changes gives about 16.79 to 17.90.
  - The 10-year average change gives about 17.38.
  - The 2021-2025 average change gives about 17.18.
- **Trend:** Oct 10 values have been low since 2023. 16.508 in 2023 is the lowest of the years I checked. Recent peaks have also come earlier, between Sep 7 and Sep 15, rather than late September.
- **Day-to-day noise:** daily values often move 0.05 to 0.2 in a day. In August 2026 they swung about 0.4 within a week.
- **Question range:** 16.5 to 18.5. Of the past 10 Oct 10 values, only 2020 (18.659) was outside it.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market, and no expert forecast, for Antarctic extent on Oct 10, 2026.
- I also found no published seasonal outlook for Antarctic extent in October.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Daily updates to the NSIDC file. The key question is when the yearly peak comes. Recently it has come around Sep 7-15, after which ice usually starts to shrink.
- NSIDC usually announces a preliminary Antarctic maximum in late September, and its early-October monthly analysis covers the September decline. [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses)
- Weather (wind patterns and storms in the Southern Ocean) caused the sharp August swings. Similar events could move extent by about 0.3-0.5 within a week.
- NSIDC's notes on the data warn that the latest daily values are preliminary and can be revised slightly.
